Waveform¶

The Wolfram Language code has support for the following waveform models:

  • IMRPhenomD: non-precessing, aligned-spin, inspiral-merger-ringdown waveform model for binary black holes (BBH), see 1508.07250 and 1508.07253.

  • IMRPhenomHM: non-precessing, aligned-spin, inspiral-merger-ringdown waveform model for BBH with higher modes, see 1708.00404.

These waveform models are implemented as functions that return the plus and cross polarizations of the GW signal, given a set of parameters.

hphcIMRPhenomD¶

hphcIMRPhenomD[f, Mc, q, s1z, s2z, iota, tc, phiRef, invdL]

Calculates the polarizations {ℎ+,ℎ×} of the IMRPhenomD approximant.

Parameters:

f: Frequency vector, where f[[i]] is in [Hz].

Mc: Chirp mass [solar mass].

q: Mass ratio in (0,1].

s1z: Aligned spin, in (-1,1).

s2z: Aligned spin, in (-1,1).

iota: Inclination angle, in [0, 𝜋].

tc: Coalescence time [s].

phiRef: Reference phase, in [0, 2 𝜋].

invdL: Inverse luminosity distance [1/Gpc].

Returns:

The polarizations {ℎ+,ℎ×} of the IMRPhenomD approximant. The output has dimensions {2, N}, where N = Length[f].

hphcIMRPhenomHM[f, Mc, q, s1z, s2z, iota, tc, phiRef, invdL]

Calculates the polarizations {ℎ+,ℎ×} of the IMRPhenomHM approximant.
